key_insight: Quantum computer rankings can change once monetary cost is included, so fidelity alone is not enough for practical backend selection.
engineering_relevance: For cloud quantum users and buyers, Quantum Fidelity-per-Cost (QFC) provides a more deployment-relevant way to compare backends across providers with different billing models.
method: Measured circuit execution fidelity across 14 cloud QPU access-path entries (12 physical QPUs) on AWS, IBM Quantum Runtime, IQM Resonance, and OQC.
Defined QFC by combining KL divergence from the ideal distribution, shot count, and monetary cost into a single score.
Analyzed how rankings and scaling behavior change under different weights and provider pricing models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a cross-provider evaluation of 14 access-path entries and shows that cost-aware rankings can differ from fidelity-only rankings.
watch_item: QFC depends on provider billing models and current prices, so scores can change as hardware and pricing policies evolve.
paper_title: Quantum Fidelity-per-Cost: A Metric for Evaluation of Quantum Computing Systems
